<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
Let $(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak R)$ be a symmetric $d$-class association scheme, and let $E_0,E_1,\ldots,E_d$ be a $Q$-polynomial ordering of its primitive idempotents. 
For $0\leqslant i\leqslant d$, write $m_i=\operatorname{rank}(E_i)$. 
Then, for all non-negative integers $a,b,c$ with $a+b+c\leqslant d$,
\begin{align}
 m_{a+b}m_{b+c}&\geqslant m_bm_{a+b+c}, \label{eq:intro-ssa}\\
 m_{a+b}m_{a+c}&\geqslant m_bm_c. \label{eq:intro-wm}
\end{align}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:bannai-ito}
Let $E_0,E_1,\ldots,E_d$ be a $Q$-polynomial ordering of the primitive idempotents of a symmetric association scheme, and write $m_i=\operatorname{rank}(E_i)$ for $0\leqslant i\leqslant d$. Then the sequence $m_0,m_1,\ldots,m_d$ is unimodal.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:stanton}
Let $E_0,E_1,\ldots,E_d$ be a $Q$-polynomial ordering of the primitive idempotents of a symmetric association scheme, and write $m_i=\operatorname{rank}(E_i)$ for $0\leqslant i\leqslant d$. Then, for each $i \in \{0,\dots,\lceil d/2\rceil-1\}$, we have
\[
 m_i\leqslant m_{i+1}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 m_i\leqslant m_{d-i}.
\]
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:Krein}
Let $0\leqslant i,j,k\leqslant d$. Then
\[
 q_{ij}^k=q_{ji}^k
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 q_{ij}^k m_k=q_{ik}^j m_j.
\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:triangle}
Let $E_0,E_1,\ldots,E_d$ be a $Q$-polynomial ordering, and let $0\leqslant i,j,k\leqslant d$. 
Then
\[
 q_{ij}^k=0
 \qquad\text{unless}\qquad
 |i-j|\leqslant k\leqslant i+j.
\]
Moreover, $q_{ij}^{i+j}>0$ whenever $i+j\leqslant d$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:entrywise-product}
Let $t$ be a positive integer and let $M_1,\ldots,M_t\in\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathfrak X}(\mathbb{R})$. Then
\[
 D_t^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
(M_1\otimes\cdots\otimes M_t)D_t
 =M_1\circ\cdots\circ M_t.
\]
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
For $x,y\in\mathfrak X$, the column of $D_t$ indexed by $x$ is the standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^{\mathfrak X^t}$ indexed by the constant tuple $(x,\ldots,x)$. Hence the $(x,y)$-entry of the left-hand side is the entry of $M_1\otimes\cdots\otimes M_t$ in row $(x,\ldots,x)$ and column $(y,\ldots,y)$, which is $\prod_{i=1}^t(M_i)_{xy}$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:F-norm}
Let $t\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$.
Suppose $E_1^{\circ t}=\sum_{k=0}^dc^{(t)}_kE_k$. Then $c^{(t)}_k\geqslant0$ for all $k$, and $c^{(t)}_k=0$ for $k>t$. 
Moreover, $c^{(t)}_t > 0$ and
\[
 E_tD_t^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
\bigl(E_1^{\otimes t}\bigr)D_tE_t=c^{(t)}_t E_t.
\]
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:entrywise-product} and the orthogonality of the primitive idempotents, we have
\[
E_tD_t^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
\bigl(E_1^{\otimes t}\bigr)D_tE_t
 =E_t\bigl(E_1^{\circ t}\bigr)E_t
 =c^{(t)}_tE_t.
\]

The remaining assertions follow by induction on $t$. The case $t=1$ is immediate. 
Suppose $t\geqslant2$.
Applying \eqref{eq:Krein-expansion}, we find that
\[
\sum_{k=0}^dc^{(t)}_kE_k = E_1^{\circ t}
=E_1\circ E_1^{\circ(t-1)} = \sum_{k=0}^d
  \left(\frac1v\sum_{j=0}^d c_j^{(t-1)}q_{1j}^k\right)E_k.
\]
Compare coefficients to obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-recursion}
 c_k^{(t)}
 =\frac1v\sum_{j=0}^d c_j^{(t-1)}q_{1j}^k.
\end{equation}
Since the Krein parameters $q_{1j}^k$ are nonnegative, we have $c_k^{(t)}\geqslant0$. 
By induction,
$c_j^{(t-1)}=0$ for $j>t-1$. 
By Proposition~\ref{prop:triangle}, if $j\leqslant t-1$ and $k>t$ then $q_{1j}^k=0$, which implies $c_k^{(t)}=0$.
Again, by Proposition~\ref{prop:triangle}, if $k=t$ then $q_{1j}^t=0$ for $j<t-1$ and $q_{1,t-1}^t>0$. Therefore,
\[
 c_t^{(t)}
 =\frac1v c_{t-1}^{(t-1)}q_{1,t-1}^{t}>0.
 \qedhere
\]
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:Ptinv}
For each $t \in \{0,\dots,d\}$, the matrix $\mathsf P_t$ is coordinate invariant.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
The case for $t = 0$ is trivial.
    For $t\geqslant1$ and $\mathbf x\in\mathfrak X^t$ and $z\in\mathfrak X$, we have
\[
 [F_t]_{\mathbf x,z}
 =\sum_{u\in\mathfrak X}\left(\prod_{i=1}^t[E_1]_{\mathbf x_i,u}\right)[E_t]_{u,z},
\]
and hence $[F_t]_{\sigma\mathbf x,z}=[F_t]_{\mathbf x,z}$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Sym}(t)$.
Since $\mathsf P_t=\alpha_t^{-1}F_tF_t^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
$, it follows that $\mathsf P_t$ is coordinate invariant.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:compatible-projections}
Let $r$ and $t$ be integers with $0\leqslant r\leqslant t\leqslant d$. 
Then
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_{t-r}(\mathsf P_t)=\frac{m_t}{m_r}\mathsf P_r.
\]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The cases $r=t$ and $r=0$ follow from the definition of partial trace and $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf P_t)=m_t$.
It suffices to prove, for each $t \in \{2,3,\dots,d\}$, that
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_1(\mathsf P_t)
 =\frac{m_t}{m_{t-1}}\mathsf P_{t-1}
\]
since the general case follows by iterating
\eqref{eq:successive-partial-traces}.

Fix $2\leqslant t\leqslant d$ and let $r=t-1$, and set $G_r:=E_1^{\otimes r}D_r$.
Then $F_r = G_rE_r$. 
By Lemma~\ref{lem:entrywise-product},
\[
 (G_rE_k)^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
(G_rE_k)
 =E_k(E_1^{\circ r})E_k
 =c_k^{(r)}E_k.
\]
By Corollary~\ref{cor:F-norm}, we have $G_rE_k=0$ whenever $k>r$.
For $\mathbf x,\mathbf y\in\mathfrak X^r$, expanding $F_t$ and using the idempotency and symmetry of $E_1$ and $E_t$ yields
\begin{align*}
 \bigl[\operatorname{Tr}_1(F_tF_t^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
)\bigr]_{\mathbf x,\mathbf y}
 &=
 \sum_{u,w\in\mathfrak X}
 [G_r]_{\mathbf x,u}[G_r]_{\mathbf y,w}[E_t]_{u,w}
 \sum_{z\in\mathfrak X}[E_1]_{z,u}[E_1]_{z,w}\\
 &=
 \bigl[G_r(E_1\circ E_t)G_r^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
\bigr]_{\mathbf x,\mathbf y}.
\end{align*}

By Proposition~\ref{prop:triangle},
$q_{1t}^k=0$ for $k<r$, since $r=t-1=|1-t|$.
Since $G_rE_k=0$ for $k>r$, we can use \eqref{eq:Krein-expansion} to obtain
\[
 G_r(E_1\circ E_t)G_r^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 

 =\frac{q_{1t}^r}{v}G_rE_rG_r^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 

 =\frac{q_{1t}^r}{v}F_rF_r^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
 =\frac{\alpha_r q_{1t}^r}{v}\mathsf P_r.
\]
Finally, we apply \eqref{eq:alpha-recursion} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:Krein} to deduce
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_1(\mathsf P_t) = \frac{1}{\alpha_t}\operatorname{Tr}_1(F_tF_t^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
)
 =
 \frac{\alpha_r q_{1t}^r}{v\alpha_t}\mathsf P_r
=
 \frac{m_t}{m_r}\mathsf P_r,
\]
as required.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:partial-trace-basic}
Let $\mathfrak X$ and $\mathfrak Y$ be finite sets and let $K\in\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathfrak X\times\mathfrak Y}(\mathbb{R})$.
If $K$ is positive semidefinite, then $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathfrak Y}(K)$ is positive semidefinite. 
Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathfrak Y}(K)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}(K).
\]
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $\{\mathbf e_z\; : \; z\in\mathfrak Y\}$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^{\mathfrak Y}$. 
For $\mathbf u\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathfrak X}$, \eqref{eq:partial-trace-general} implies
\[
 \mathbf u^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 
\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathfrak Y}(K)\mathbf u
 =
 \sum_{z\in\mathfrak Y}
 (\mathbf u\otimes\mathbf e_z)^ 
  {\mathpalette\@transpose{}} 

 K(\mathbf u\otimes\mathbf e_z),
\]
which is non-negative when $K$ is positive semidefinite.
The trace identity follows since
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathfrak Y}(K)\bigr)
 =
 \sum_{x\in\mathfrak X}\sum_{z\in\mathfrak Y}
 K_{(x,z),(x,z)}
 =
 \operatorname{Tr}(K). \qedhere
\]
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Let $a,b,c$ be non-negative integers with $t:=a+b+c\leqslant d$.
The case $t=0$ is immediate, so suppose that $t\geqslant1$.
Set
\[
 \mathfrak X_1:=\mathfrak X^a,\qquad
 \mathfrak X_2:=\mathfrak X^b,\qquad
 \mathfrak X_3:=\mathfrak X^c.
\]
We consider $\mathsf P_t$ as a matrix with rows and columns indexed by $\mathfrak X_1\times\mathfrak X_2\times\mathfrak X_3$ under its natural bijection with $\mathfrak X^t$.

For $J\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$, write
$\overline{J}:=\{1,2,3\}\setminus J$ and
\[
 \mathfrak X_J:=\prod_{j\in J}\mathfrak X_j,
\]
where the factors $\mathfrak X_j$ occur in their natural order and $\mathfrak X_\emptyset$ is a singleton.
Observe that $m_t^{-1}\mathsf P_t$ is a density matrix.
Define
\[
 S_J:=h\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{\overline{J}}(m_t^{-1}\mathsf P_t)\bigr).
\]
Lieb and Ruskai (see \cite[Theorem~2(i),(ii)]{LiebRuskai}
and \cite[(3.1) and (3.2)]{Pippenger}) showed that
\begin{align}
 S_{\{1,2,3\}}+S_{\{2\}}
 &\leqslant S_{\{1,2\}}+S_{\{2,3\}},
 \label{eq:strong-subadditivity}\\
 S_{\{2\}}+S_{\{3\}}
 &\leqslant S_{\{1,2\}}+S_{\{1,3\}}.
 \label{eq:weak-monotonicity}
\end{align}


Fix $J\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$, and let $j$ be the total number of individual coordinates in the blocks indexed by $J$.
Move these blocks to the front, preserving their natural order and the coordinate order within each block, followed by the
remaining blocks in their natural order.
This is a permutation of the $t$ individual coordinates, under which $\mathsf P_t$ is unchanged by Lemma~\ref{lem:Ptinv}.

Then identifying $\mathfrak X_J$ with $\mathfrak X^j$ by concatenation, the definition of partial trace and
Theorem~\ref{thm:compatible-projections} together yield
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_{\overline{J}}(m_t^{-1}\mathsf P_t)
 =\operatorname{Tr}_{t-j}(m_t^{-1}\mathsf P_t)
 =m_j^{-1}\mathsf P_j.
\]
This reduced density matrix has exactly $m_j$ non-zero eigenvalues, all equal to $1/m_j$.
Hence, $S_J=\log m_j$.

Substitute the expressions for $S_J$ into \eqref{eq:strong-subadditivity} and \eqref{eq:weak-monotonicity} to obtain
\begin{align*}
 \log m_{a+b+c}+\log m_b
 &\leqslant\log m_{a+b}+\log m_{b+c},\\
 \log m_b+\log m_c
 &\leqslant\log m_{a+b}+\log m_{a+c}.
\end{align*}
Exponentiating completes the proof.
